propositions: A Jira issue's KEY changes when moved between projects while its numeric id is stable, so bindings keyed on the KEY can silently detach and orphan a local ticket when the old key stops resolving.
The absence probe reads a no-longer-resolving key as gone and retires a binding for an issue that still exists.

The fix additively records the numeric jira_id on each binding and, on a key-lookup miss, re-resolves by id and re-keys the binding to the issue's current key while updating the reverse index in the same operation.

The change must leave all existing jira_key-taking methods unchanged in signature and semantics because the binding store is shared with the Cloud bridge, and legacy bindings without a recorded id must keep working with no migration.
The id fallback must not fire while the key still resolves, and a genuine deletion must still retire rather than being masked as a re-key.

Measured on real DC 8.17.1, GET on a stale/old key after a project key rename returns 200 with the new key in the body, so the id fallback on 404 is a safety net for the KB-documented case where a third-party mover fails to update moved_issue_key.
